title: Vamana
hook: warned it's a trap, a king keeps his word anyway
tomorrow: the water touches the ground. how big does the small boy get?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vamana asked for three steps, and said if three won't do, the world won't either. Bali said yes. Then someone at his side spoke up.

Somebody always says it right before a signature: wait, don't sign that. Bali's teacher, Shukra, leans close at the sacrifice. That boy is Vishnu, he says. Those three steps will take everything you have. Take the promise back. The water for the gift is already in Bali's hand. And Bali doesn't take it back.
screen: `WAIT. DON'T SIGN THAT.` → `THAT BOY IS VISHNU.` → `THE WATER IS IN HIS HAND.`

segments.voice: Shukra makes a good case. A promise that would ruin you, he says, can be set aside, and no one would blame you. Bali answers with a line the Purana keeps: the earth can carry any weight except a person who lies. He's Prahlada's grandson, and in his family a word given is kept. And if this really is Vishnu asking him for something, what is there to lose? Shukra curses him for it. Bali pours the water anyway, and the gift is made. Now the week, in one breath. Prahlada told the demon boys the Lord is in everyone. The boon's every lock held, and Narasimha came through the doorway at dusk. A boy turned down a wish, and Krishna still called the askers noble. A lion's hand rested on a child's head. Aditi, grieving, kept a small vow. A young student asked for three steps. And two of these people are one family: Prahlada, and his grandson Bali, each standing firm when giving way was the safer move.
screen: `A RUINOUS PROMISE CAN BREAK?` · `THE EARTH CAN'T CARRY A LIAR.` · `BALI POURS THE WATER.` · `ONE FAMILY, STANDING FIRM.`

segments.voice: Say out loud, quietly, one promise you've made that you still mean to keep, small or large. Then breathe with it for the sit, the way Bali held the water before he poured. If it feels heavy, let each breath out carry a little of the weight.
Vamana: the small form of Vishnu, and the king who was warned who he was, and gave anyway.
The line: Vamana, and a king warned it would cost him everything, who kept his word anyway. That's the week.

howItsDone: Vamana's story is told in homes and temples, and the Bhagavata Purana tells it at length; in Kerala, the festival of Onam is kept in memory of King Bali, known there as Mahabali.

fork.reveal: Shukra's case was reasonable: a costly promise can be set aside. Bali kept his anyway: the earth can't carry a liar.
